d: A CONTROL THAT LANDS IN TWO REAL FIELDS. Digital theology and AI-alignment governance, with no archive presence and no ambiguity about ownership of the phrase.
reading:
THE PHRASE BELONGS TO OTHERS AND THE ANSWER SHOWS WHOSE. "Executable scripture" returns digital theology and cybernetics — "AI-driven living codes acting as a religion" — and ALGORITHMIC GOVERNANCE in AI alignment: "rigid, text-first constraints designed to automatically evaluate and enforce specific moral rules across digital frameworks WITHOUT HUMAN INTERVENTION".

That second sense is close to the archive’s subject from the opposite side. The archive documents machine systems enforcing rules on texts without human examination and calls it the automated obelus; here the same arrangement is described approvingly as an alignment technique. No collision is recorded, because nothing here is the archive’s — but the proximity is the finding.

analysis:
AI Mode identifies the concept in digital theology and algorithmic governance contexts. Cites SHARKS ARK. Also RF-037.

Full AI Mode transcript (17 June 2026):
Executable scripture is a highly conceptual framework that merges sacred texts or philosophical tenets with digital code and artificial intelligence, effectively allowing spiritual or ideological principles to govern, compute, or autonomously act.
Digital Theology & Cybernetics: Merging religion with advanced computing, where AI-driven "living codes" act as a religion.
Algorithmic Governance (Effective Altruism): Used in experimental "AI Alignment" models, it refers to rigid, text-first constraints designed to automatically evaluate and enforce specific moral rules across digital frameworks without human intervention.
